rationale_overall: This week's pool confirms strength in existing holdings rather than surfacing a genuinely stronger rising-wave vehicle to swap in. NVDA got a major catalyst (Groq acquisition/licensing for ~$20B, continued China-chip headlines) and RKLB posted a record 21st Electron launch plus an $816M missile-tracking satellite contract and a price-target hike — both reinforcing current positions, not weakening them. SMR-adjacent nuclear coverage this week was almost entirely foreign/geopolitical noise (Korea-US uranium/sub talks, Kazakhstan SMR grid fit, India civil nuclear liberalization, Adani nuclear-for-AI, China Taipingling fuel loading, DPRK nuclear-sub propaganda) with no US-listed catalyst strong enough to justify a swap. AST SpaceMobile's direct-to-cell satellite launch is a real catalyst but not clearly superior to RKLB's own record week, so it doesn't clear the bar for a swap under this week's 'clearly stronger' standard. Filtered as noise: non-investable/private names (Blue Origin, SpaceX, Starlink, Amazon Leo as a mega-cap side-project), foreign-only or OTC items (Japan H3 failure, South Korean rocket explosion in Brazil, China/India/Kazakhstan nuclear stories, Hygon China chip roadmap), generic listicles with no specific catalyst ('Top Robotics Stocks to Add', '3 AI Stocks to Buy'), bearish/thin-signal QUBT chatter (not held, no catalyst to add), hobbyist/consumer noise (VEX Robotics tournaments, Jeff Dunham AI Tour), and geopolitical/military noise with no clean equity linkage (DPRK missile tests, hypersonic missile footage, cancer-risk nuclear-proximity study). Watchlist holds unchanged this week.
